variables.name: participant_id
variables.label: Study participant ID
variables.notes: A random study code assigned by the research team. Never use a student ID number, email, or name. Keep the linking key separately from the data, and replace these codes with new random codes before sharing.

variables.name: timepoint
variables.label: Data collection timepoint
variables.notes: For long-format data. In wide-format data, use the _pre / _post / _t1 ... suffixes on variable names instead.

variables.name: age_years
variables.label: Age in years
variables.question: What is your age in years?
variables.notes: Consider collecting or sharing age in ranges, and top-coding older ages, to reduce re-identification risk.

variables.name: race_eth
variables.label: Race and/or ethnicity (combined question)
variables.question: What is your race and/or ethnicity?
variables.source: OMB Statistical Policy Directive No. 15 (2024), minimum reporting categories
variables.notes: Each option is stored as its own 0/1 variable (race_eth_aian, race_eth_asian, ...). SPD 15 also calls for detailed categories and write-in fields under each minimum category; add those as study-specific variables when collected. 'Prefer not to answer' is a HuMeta addition, not an SPD 15 category. Small groups can identify individuals: check cell sizes before sharing.

variables.name: consent_share
variables.label: Consented to data sharing
variables.question: Do you agree that your de-identified responses may be shared with other researchers?
variables.notes: Only participants coded 1 may be included in any shared dataset. Wording must match the IRB-approved consent form.

variables.name: gender_identity
variables.label: Gender identity
variables.source: ICPSR Social Science Variables Database (search and compare variables)
variables.notes: Linked entry: the name is fixed so studies match, but the question wording and answer codes are not set here. See how other studies ask it in ICPSR's variables database (open the ICPSR term and choose Search for this term), and record the wording and codes you use in your codebook. The National Academies (2022) recommend a two-step measure: sex assigned at birth, then current gender. Small groups can identify people: check cell sizes before sharing.

variables.name: first_gen
variables.label: First-generation college student
variables.source: ICPSR Social Science Variables Database (search and compare variables)
variables.notes: Linked entry: the name is fixed so studies match, but the question wording and answer codes are not set here. See how other studies ask it in ICPSR's variables database (open the ICPSR term and choose Search for this term), and record the wording and codes you use in your codebook. Definitions vary; say which you use. The Higher Education Act definition: neither parent (or, for a student who lived with and was supported by one parent, that parent) completed a bachelor's degree.

variables.name: class_standing
variables.label: Class standing (year in college)
variables.source: ICPSR Social Science Variables Database (search and compare variables)
variables.notes: Linked entry: the name is fixed so studies match, but the question wording and answer codes are not set here. See how other studies ask it in ICPSR's variables database (open the ICPSR term and choose Search for this term), and record the wording and codes you use in your codebook. For the student's year (first-year, second-year, ...). The level of the course is a separate variable, course_level.

variables.name: major_cip
variables.label: Major or field of study (CIP code)
variables.source: ICPSR Social Science Variables Database (search and compare variables)
variables.notes: Linked entry: record the six-digit CIP 2020 code of the student's major in the form ##.#### (for example 26.0205, Molecular Biology). The first two digits group related programs. See how other studies ask about major in ICPSR's variables database. Small majors can identify people: share the two-digit series if cells are small.
